title: Field Facilitator Compact Workshop Kit
body:
Purpose:
- Lightweight, transportable facilitator kit for 1-day customer integration accelerator.
- Goal: validate integration approach, capture latency/cost envelope, align on MVP acceptance criteria and next-steps.

Audience:
- 2–6 customer engineers (app + infra), 1 product manager, 1 security/contact.
- Redwood attendees: 1 solutions engineer (facilitator), 1 infra/ops engineer (float), 1 customer success observer.

Prework for customer (send 3 days before):
- Provide sample API key or sandbox credentials (hosted or dedicated sim).
- Share 2 canonical prompts / request patterns and a representative corpus (<= 500 docs).
- Brief network diagram + IAM boundaries for integration conversation.
- Fill short intake form: performance targets (p95 latency), throughput, compliance constraints.

Day agenda (compact 7.5 hours):
- 09:00–09:20 Introductions & success criteria (facilitator) — quick expectations, review intake form.
- 09:20–09:50 Tech context & constraints (customer) — app flow, infra, security blockers.
- 09:50–10:10 Redwood runtime overview (15m) + Q/A (5m) — focused on routing, caching, fallbacks.
- 10:10–10:25 Quick break (15m)
- 10:25–11:40 Hands-on integration sprint (part 1) — wire up sample call, verify auth, get first generation.
  - Tasks: exchange test payloads, run single-call, capture logs/traces.
- 11:40–12:20 Latency & cost sketching session — review tokenization, batching options, budget tradeoffs.
- 12:20–13:10 Lunch
- 13:10–14:30 Hands-on integration sprint (part 2) — KV/prefix caching, streaming, and retry policies.
  - Try small A/B: cached vs no-cache 100 reqs.
- 14:30–15:00 Breakout: failure modes & graceful degradation (roles: dev, ops)
- 15:00–15:40 Canary + rollback & monitoring blueprint (Redwood console demo)
- 15:40–16:10 Acceptance criteria: define MVP rollout gating (quality buckets, latency SLOs, cost thresholds)
- 16:10–16:40 Next-step mapping & responsibilities (who does what by when)
- 16:40–17:00 Wrap, open issues, and parking lot

Slide outline (compact deck, ~12 slides):
1: Title + day objectives (1 slide) — bold success criteria up top.
2: Customer context summary (1 slide) — app flow diagram, traffic shape.
3: Redwood quick-architecture (1 slide) — routing tiers, model variants, deployment modes.
4: Integration checklist (1 slide) — creds, endpoints, network, CORS, latency hooks.
5: Live demo plan & tasks (1 slide) — what we will run during sprints.
6: Observability & telemetry hooks (1 slide) — logs, tracing keys, token cost metrics.
7: Batching & caching primer (1 slide) — when to use each, quick heuristics.
8: Failure patterns & mitigation (1 slide) — e.g., OOM, kv-miss, auth failures.
9: Canary & rollback play (1 slide) — rollout %, health checks.
10: Acceptance criteria template (1 slide) — concrete thresholds for MVP.
11: Post-day deliverables & timeline (1 slide) — PoC report, infra runbook, follow-up sync.
12: Parking lot & contact sheet (1 slide)

Facilitator notes (cheat-style):
- Keep demos short: aim for 5–8 minute demo cycles. If stuck, switch to whiteboard explanation and mark follow-up item.
- Record p95/p50/p99 and token counts for every test scenario — these are the most actionable metrics for customers.
- Encourage customer engineers to run the first end-to-end call — ownership is key.
- Watch for network/firewall issues early: common blocker that kills momentum.
- Use the A/B comparison to make quant tradeoffs tangible: e.g., caching reduced token cost by X% in our internal tests.
- Capture exact prompts used and model+config so results are reproducible.

Interactive exercises (short):
- Exercise A: Prompt robustness quick-check (10m) — 5 sample prompts, track hallucinations, false-positives, confidence.
- Exercise B: Cost vs latency matrix (20m) — group sorts three profiles by priority, pick recommended config.
- Exercise C: Incident roleplay (15m) — simulate model unavailability and test fallback route.

Prep checklist (for SE before customer day):
- Verify sandbox credentials and pre-populated test data.
- Run the demo script end-to-end on the same network band customer will use.
- Create 3 docs in shared drive: 'demo-requests.txt', 'expected-responses.md', 'metrics-template.csv'.
- Pre-seed Redwood console with a model variant and attach tracing keys.
- Prepare 2 quick fallback model variants (lower-cost and beefier) to demo routing.

Common risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Customer network blocks outbound connections. Mitigation: bring a local laptop hotspot or demo via recorded trace + post-day follow up.
- Risk: Missing sample corpus. Mitigation: have synthetic generator script (small) to create representative payloads.
- Risk: Expectations mismatch on quality. Mitigation: run a quick blind eval with customer-provided prompts and show quality matrix.

Outputs to deliver within 48 hours:
- Short PoC recap (1–2 pages) with measurements (latency, token cost) and acceptance criteria.
- Runbook: steps to reproduce tests (credentials, commands, expected outputs).
- Action list: owners + dates for integration, infra, security items.

Notes to self / rough ideas to capture for iteration:
- Could add a tiny latency sandbox that simulates on-prem network characteristics (if customer is private/VPC).
- Keep a lightweight consent doc for recording demos (customers sometimes ask).
- Consider a 30m follow-up focused solely on security/infrastructure blockers after PoC recap.

Revision history: 
- 2025-02-14 first draft (Priya)
- 2025-02-20 added A/B sprint tasks and metrics-template (Marco)
- 2025-03-01 updated mitigation plan and outputs (Aisha)

Parking lot / unanswered questions (to resolve before final):
- Will customer require HIPAA-level logs redaction? If yes, need legal sign-off + longer timeline.
- Does the customer prefer canary percentage increments automated or manual?

End of kit.
